title: Levonorgestrel synergistically potentiates lenvatinib-induced cytotoxicity in human hepatocellular carcinoma PLC/PRF/5 cells via inhibiting the PI3K/Akt pathway and triggering ROS-mediated apoptosis
content:
Abstract
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly lethal malignancy worldwide, and the clinical efficacy of first-line targeted agent lenvatinib is limited by acquired drug resistance and suboptimal monotherapeutic outcomes. This study examined the synergistic cytotoxicity and underlying mechanism of levonorgestrel combined with lenvatinib in human HCC PLC/PRF/5 cells. Cell viability and synergism (combination index, CI) were determined by CCK-8 assay and Chou–Talalay method. Proliferation, migration, apoptosis and intracellular ROS were evaluated via functional assays and flow cytometry. Core drug-disease targets and pathways were screened by network pharmacology, and PI3K/Akt phosphorylation was validated by Western blotting. Combined treatment significantly suppressed cell viability, proliferation and migration, induced apoptosis and ROS accumulation, with all CI values below 0.6 indicating strong synergism. The ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine (NAC) markedly reversed these combinatory effects. 153 overlapping targets were identified, mainly enriched in the PI3K/Akt pathway. Combination treatment significantly downregulated phosphorylated PI3K and Akt without total protein changes versus control and monotherapy groups. Akt activator SC79 significantly attenuated the ROS elevation and cell viability inhibition induced by the two-drug combination. In conclusion, levonorgestrel synergistically potentiates lenvatinib-induced cytotoxicity in HCC cells by inhibiting PI3K/Akt activation and triggering ROS-mediated apoptosis.
